Summary (full text)

Camera eufy-t40xp-sc830 (T40) in the light box with the SpyderCheckr 24 chart, lamps 3000 K. Both stacks ran on the same camera, the same chart position and the same light: the open stack (open-tx-isp + OpenIMP + timps) and the vendor stack (Ingenic ISP module + vendor libimp + timps built for it), one after the other.

Result: 59 pass, 15 fail (9 invalid by test setup, 1 vendor difference, 5 issues), 111 info/warn, 1 flaky (failed 1 of 3, repeated), 1 planned checks not run in these runs.

Failed checks: H.264 FixQP 25: decodes clean (open 2, vendor 0; decode errors (ffmpeg -v error); pass = 0 on open); H.264 FixQP 35: decodes clean (open 2, vendor 0; decode errors (ffmpeg -v error); pass = 0 on open); H.264 CBR 1000: decodes clean (open 2, vendor 0; decode errors (ffmpeg -v error); pass = 0 on open); H.264 CBR 2000: decodes clean (open 2, vendor 0; decode errors (ffmpeg -v error); pass = 0 on open); H.265 FixQP 25: decodes clean (open 2, vendor 0; decode errors (ffmpeg -v error); pass = 0 on open); H.265 FixQP 35: decodes clean (open 2, vendor 0; decode errors (ffmpeg -v error); pass = 0 on open); H.265 CBR 2000: decodes clean (open 2, vendor 0; decode errors (ffmpeg -v error); pass = 0 on open); H.265 CBR 2000: SSIM mean / min (open 0.9709 / 0.9680, vendor 0.9759 / 0.9748; pass = open mean >= vendor - 0.005).

Warnings: H.264 FixQP 25: blocking / ghosting flags (open blk 1.35, decode errors, blocking (border/inner step +0.35 > 0.10), vendor blk 1.39, blocking (border/inner step +0.39 > 0.10)): blk = 8-px border/inner step of the error image (1.00 = none); How to read: "pass" means the open stack is equal to or better than the vendor stack within the tolerance named in each row; matched-exposure rows (A2) compare the same integration time and gain on both stacks, read back from the ISP.

A5 Encoder (H.264 / H.265): open vs vendor, same settings

Cells = open / vendor. Static chart scene, lamps on, day pinned, streamer restarted per case with a /tmp conf. Bytes per frame and P/I from ffprobe -show_frames (frames before the first IDR and, for CBR, the first seconds are ignored). PSNR / SSIM (luma) of every decoded frame (SSIM every 4th) against the mean image of the stack's own H.264 FixQP reference recording, so the ISP difference between the stacks drops out; sensor noise stays in (see the noise-floor row): an encoder that smooths noise can score higher than the reference. blk = blockiness of the error image (step across 8-px borders / step inside, 1.00 = no block structure); GOP drift = PSNR of the IDR minus the last P of the GOP. n/a = the streamer of that stack did not take the setting.

Method

  • Same camera, same chart position, same lamps; open stack first, then the vendor ISP module + vendor libimp are loaded from /tmp (nothing flashed); the camera returns to the flashed image at the end (module reload or reboot).
  • P1 = camera defaults (AE, AWB, comp 128). P2 = matched exposure: the same integration time and gains on both stacks, set inside the streamer and read back from the ISP; rows whose read-back differs are marked verify=FAIL and not compared.
  • A/A: point p2_a is measured twice (p2_a, p2_a2); the relative difference is the repeatability of the method. A difference between the stacks counts only beyond 2 x that spread (floor 5 %).
  • NV12 noise is measured on raw NV12 frames from the streamer (no JPEG in the path): temporal standard deviation per pixel over the burst, mean over Y 32..224, and U/V.
  • Colour: SpyderCheckr 24 detected automatically, sRGB -> Lab (D50), CIEDE2000 against the Datacolor default values (D50 assumed, not batch specific); 'grey-normalised' removes the white-balance cast first.
  • Sharpness: slanted-edge method on the chart's outer patch edges, frames averaged against noise; JPEG snapshot path.
  • SSIM/PSNR (when run): both stacks record the same static chart scene at the same bitrate; each stream is decoded and compared against a high-bitrate capture of the SAME stack (reference), so the number is the encoder loss of that stack; a cross-stack comparison on static frames is listed separately and includes the ISP difference.
  • Encoder (A5): both stacks get the same timps settings (codec, rc_mode, qp / bitrate, gop) through a /tmp conf and a streamer restart; the recordings come over RTSP (ffmpeg -c copy). The reference is a mean image, because single NV12 frames are not frame-aligned with the stream; the scene is static, so every decoded frame can be compared with it. A second reference at the end of the phase shows whether the scene or the AE moved in between.
  • Lamp switches are made by a person on a marker (NEED_* file); the times above are the marker times.
